paper_metadata.title: Ambient and elevated temperature mechanical behavior of Mg-Gd-Cu-Zr alloy

evidence.quote: The Mg-6.0Gd-1.2Cu-1.2Zr (wt%) alloy was designed, then processed by solution treatment, as well as the following single-aging and double-aging treatments respectively.

The Mg-6.0Gd-1.2Cu-1.2Zr (wt%) alloy was prepared by gravity casting, using pure Mg(99.99%), Mg-30Gd (wt%), Mg-30Cu (wt%) and Mg-30Zr (wt%) master alloys. These raw materials were melted under a protective atmosphere of mixed CO2 and SF6 gas. After mechanical stirred and maintained at 720°C for 20 min, the molten metals were poured into the molds.
The ingots were solution treated at 350°C and 440 °C under a protective SO2 atmosphere

82.0%– 98.8% yield strength retention of the alloy under various conditions is detected at 150 °Ca s compared to the yield strength at room temperature.
This means that the single-aging treatment and double-aging treatment can effectively generate aging strengthening mechanism.

The Alloy B with more volume fraction of LPSO structure shows the lower yield strength than the as-cast alloy, indicating that LPSO structure strengthening is weaken while the strength reduction caused by grain growth plays a dominate role.
The negative effect cause by grain growth plays a more predominating role than solution strengthening in the solution-treated alloy, and hence the YS is still lower than Alloy A.
